### 2026-10-26: # Started researching Ideas

**5.1h**

# Started researching Ideas

So after designing the curtain opener for my week 1 and 2 projects, I figured that it would be good to continue in the same direction, and try to make something else automated. Then I decided, why not make the thing that automated everything.

So I decided to make a SmartHome Dashboard and controller.

## The Plan

I want to use an E-ink display, as they look really fancy, and are meant to be really low power. I'll use some sort of MCU to control it, probably an esp32s3, so it could be used standalone if needed. However, I plan to also include some sort of SBC capable of running something like home assistant.

So my original plan was to make it fully solar powered, but after finding out the battery draw of SBC's, I've come to the annoying conclusion that the solar power will have to be a backup, or at least supplemented with mains. Also would like to make the solar panel track the sun, but unsure if I will have the budget for this.

## My progress

### 2026-10-27: # Found a Solar Panel

**1.7h**

# Found a Solar Panel

Started researching them a while ago. But finally found a solar panel I was happy with.

## My tangent with bare cells

So from research, I read that managing bare solar panels is a slight pain, as the voltage can fluctuate a lot. But I was willing to give it a try. So I looked at bare cells:

![10599](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/a14ce0983a036f86b7c5921f84b297c0ff4aef12a646c60eea33680c37d5b950.png)

~$9 for a single 5w 5v panel seemed steep, but it is what it is, so then I looked into MPPT boards, which seemed complex, but not too bad. So I found one in the end that I was happy with.

Then I looked again at solar panels and realised I can just get the phone charging ones. That dont need extra boards

## The result

I'm now planning to get a 30W, yes 30W panel - still monocrystalline, but it will output a stable 5v through usb. Not really sure how this will work, as I thought USB-A only went up to 18W. But we'll have to see. Worse case I just cut the wires a bit.

![10598](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/3f7db29ce2833b32e4449fb8e7f3a0758e9a0395c045858de9c96a021499f75c.png)

And it's also fairly cheap, at $14 - which is less than the bare panel and charging circuitry needed for the bare panel route.

So anyway, I'll have to charge that into an 18650 charging module, and I'll also try to put like a MOSFET in, so I can cap the charge when the battery hits 80%.

But having a 30W panel should make it quite quick.

## tl;dr

Figured out a pre made solar panel charging setup would be more cost effective, and have somehow ended up with a 30w panel.

### 2026-10-28: # Made some hard decisions

**4.97h**

# Made some hard decisions

## Yet more Research

So annoyingly, this project is mostly going to be spent on research, especially in the design phase. But I guess its still working on it, just not exactly doing anything fancy.

So as I want to make the display able to run and update indefinitely, I figured I needed some sort of battery management system.

So my current thinking:

![10718](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/525047ab25919b262d1abac59833027dfff03a0991f5d1fb52c6ec2594a8216d.png)

I've already ordered a few of these batteries, as I know they definitely won't fit in the BOM, and as they seem to have a really high capacity - 3500mAh 18650s. Never heard of EVE 35V before though. Had to order them anyway, as delibery is like £15 and like a month - I'm ordering from nkon as somehow it's still cheaper than UK?

![10719](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8811816c8272a3d47fdae2c79554c50fddc6e734913a5f29767d3196d6a40ac7.png)

So anyway, I plan to use 2 or mabye 4 cells to make a bank of say (3500x2) 7000mAh, so with say a nominal voltage of 3.6V as shown in the specs, that'll give me 25.2Wh of battery life.

### Napkin math

So with rough math:
- the pi will use like 3W max
- MCU and screen probably like less than 0.1W
- Solar panel can do 30w, but will probably be more like 15W for like 5 hours in the day, so can charge, say, so 20W for 5h or 100Wh total.

Multiplying those for a 24h period
- pi 3x24 is 72Wh
-  MCU and screen 0.1x24 is 2.4Wh
-  total consumed is like 74.4Wh
-  total produced is 100Wh

So have a 33% overhead, which should account for cloudy days and other hardware losses.

###  Not doing fully solar though

But anyway, I don't plan to run it purely on solar, just due to the uncertainty, as all it needs is like two cloudy days in a row, and then it's gonna run flat. Which from researching about the pi, is really bad, as them the data on the micro SD card corrupts and I've got to set it up again from scratch.

So I plan to primarily use solar, but have mains as a backup. I guess it could also be reversed, so have mains as the main power path, then batteries and solar as more of a ups style option. But it should also work fully off grid I think.

### Power preference?

So when I was looking into it, for the solar, it'll obviously output whatever it can, but then the problems arise in figuring out how to divert the power.

This is as the pi needs to get a stable voltage and current. And I ideally don't want to micro charge the batteries, so that means the solar needs a bypass, and a possible battery supplement. But then when there's enough juice, the pi needs power and the batteries can charge.

So from too much research, I think I can do it with a bunch of MOSFETs. So my plan is to use a current sensing module like say the ina219.

![10720](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/0ece487b5db0f855de93c3ae3a2ee2ecf098d31759f1c36236af84e5674927b2.png)

So I could use the ina219 to sense the charging current, and read it though the esp32. Then I could use a series of MOSFETs to have it turned off when not enough voltage or current is coming through, or turn it on to say let power to only the battery, only the pi, or to both.

Then I think I could have another set of MOSFETs on the other side to then figure out what power is going into the pi from both the batteries and the solar. These will both obviously have to go into a boost converter, as I plan to do the batteries in series. But before then, I guess I'll have to have them switch on or off somehow.

But anyway, as I also plan to implement a mains backup, from what I've read up on, I can just connect it with MOSFETs so I can toggle things, but from what I've read, I can also set the voltage a tiny bit lower than the boost converter, so the pi pulls the high voltage line when it's there, and automatically falls back to the other one otherwise. But I'll have to do more research into that.

I'm pretty sure that I'll also have to put like diodes at every step with the amount of power things that could go backwards.

Also the MOSFETs might be a bit annoying, especially regarding the charging paths, as I plan to toggle the live wires - not ground, but that means I'll either have to do it through a resistor, or use both an n channel and a p channel MOSFET to close voltage lines higher than the esp32's 3.3v line. I've spent way to long looking into that, and I still don't fully understand it.

![10722](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e7bf85d0a7f86e4434d6c3eb31809310b8dd66eed63ad6a7b88faa932cb67c45.jpg)

### Batt charging

So from looking, I've landed in the CC/CV lm2596 buck converter to charge it, as it can take the 5v in, and charge the batteries at the current I set, probably like 2A, then I can also set the voltage limit - will probably use 4V, as that should prolong the cell lifetime, as it's only about 80% then. And can use a voltage divider to monitor them. Will be in parallel, so I don't need to worry about cell balancing etc.

![10723](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/0da5fd7e0190d99a8ad0356c16975481c148ca41d4b0240b23eb34549b6364c6.jpg)

## tl;dr

I think it might actually be possible to make this fully off grid. I'll try to do it this way, but will include a mains backup just in case. And just spent this entire session trying to figure out how I would do this.
